title: Relational background field formulation of discrete quantum gravity models: The case of $O(N)$ vector models in zero dimensions
authors: Vincent Lahoche, Dine Ousmane Samary, Parham Radpay
abstract: In a recent paper arxiv.org/abs/2609.21031, we have introduced the concept of a relational background field as a new approach to the renormalization group (RG) for discrete quantum gravity models, focusing on random matrix models. The proposed method offers the dual advantage of preserving the model's gauge symmetry (typically $U(N)$ or $O(N)$), whose breaking in conventional approaches has remained an open problem, and providing a more satisfactory treatment of the continuum or infrared (IR) limit. In this limit, the theory is described by a non-local field theory in dimension $D = 2k + 3$, where $k$ denotes the number of cuts in the effective spectrum as dictated by random matrix theory. This pedagogical paper reviews this construction for real random vector models in zero dimensions, with $O(N)$ as the symmetry group. Following the general strategy of background-field-type formulations, we show, using the BBP (Baik-Ben Arrous-P'ech'e) phase transition, that a partial Hubbard--Stratonovich decomposition of the quartic interaction, involving a matrix-valued intermediate field, allows a preferred notion of scale to emerge. This scale, in turn, defines an RG flow, whose perturbative structure is analyzed. Our calculation demonstrates the existence of an \textit{asymptotic} Wilson--Fisher-type fixed point, whose sole relevant critical exponent is in qualitative agreement with the double-scaling critical exponent of these models.
summary: This paper introduces a relational background field formulation as a new Renormalization Group technique for discrete quantum gravity models, particularly random matrix theories. By utilizing the $O(N)$ model, the authors show how this method preserves gauge symmetry while defining a stable RG flow. The key finding is the existence of an asymptotic Wilson-Fisher fixed point, offering a controlled path to the continuum limit.
main_problem: Developing a reliable Renormalization Group (RG) approach for discrete quantum gravity models while preserving the underlying gauge symmetry and achieving a satisfactory continuum limit.
main_result: The authors demonstrate the existence of an asymptotic Wilson-Fisher-type fixed point using a novel relational background field formulation.
method: The method employs a relational background field formulation combined with a partial Hubbard-Stratonovich decomposition to define an RG flow based on the BBP phase transition.
model_or_system: The study focuses on random matrix models, specifically the $O(N)$ vector model in zero dimensions, which serves as a pedagogical review of the general construction.
key_observables: Asymptotic Wilson-Fisher fixed point, relevant critical exponent, free energy singularity exponent (gamma=1/2).
important_parameters: Large N limit, $O(N)$ symmetry, BBP phase transition, dimension $D=2k+3$.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the self-averaging property for large random matrices and is presented as a review of the construction.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the relational background field concept, reviews its application to the $O(N)$ model, details the use of the BBP transition to define the RG flow, and analyzes the resulting fixed point structure.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum gravity, the rigorous application of RG techniques, fixed-point analysis, and symmetry preservation in the large-N limit provides advanced theoretical tools applicable to critical phenomena in complex many-body systems.
